$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ 4x+3y\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $T(kv)=kT(v)$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vector $v$ and real scalar $k$

II. $T({v}_{1}+{v}_{2})=T({v}_{1})+T({v}_{2})$ for any real $2\times 1$ column vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$

III. $T$ is a linear transformation", "field_keys": ["selection"]}]
question.worked_solution:
q-12008:
A linear transformation $T$ satisfies two properties:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}]=kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}], \\  & T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the first condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}kx \\ ky\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}kx+ky \\ 4kx+3ky\end{aligned}] \\  & =k[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ 4x+3y\end{aligned}] \\  & =kT[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Checking the second condition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{y}_{1}+{y}_{2} \\ 4({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})+3({y}_{1}+{y}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{y}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}+{y}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2}+3{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {y}_{1}\end{aligned}]+T[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{T}$ is a linear transformation.

As a result, all three statements are true.
